description:
## Goal

Rebuild the recalculator stack on the exact accepted PR #121 and #122 histories, exclude invalid PR #123, and make the first real simplification on that clean base: delete the unused per-derivation scheduler substrate.

The stack transition and first implementation are one atomic ticket. A branch identical to #122 cannot produce a meaningful reviewable PR, and a padding commit would be construction debris.

## Stack boundary

- Preserve current .200/.220 working material and parked candidates only as recoverable research; do not land them wholesale.
- Close PR #123 as invalid. Neither fz-kdt.214 nor fz-kdt.75 is carried as architecture.
- Keep PR #121 as the denotational-list predecessor.
- Reconcile PR #122 onto the exact accepted #121 head. PR #122 contains fz-kdt.183, .199, .210 and other closed prerequisites required by the revised semantic plan.
- Refresh PR #121's body against its actual accepted head. At planning, the body proves obsolete pre-rebase commit 67e09d37311b while the sole current commit is c35a4bead818; verification provenance must name the commit reviewers will merge.
- Refresh PR #122's body from its exact final diff and head. At planning, it describes only the first few of 50 commits and an early 1960/561 census; the replacement must explain the full accepted runtime-library arc and current proof without stale counts.
- PR #124 remains independent concordant cleanup and may land separately. Its dangling deleted-ticket identities and PR-title defect are owned by fz-tt2 and do not enter this stack ticket.
- Create a clean recalculator branch above accepted #122 containing neither rejected #123 commit.
- Before closing, use gh stacks to adopt and submit the remote stack in exact order: main -> #121 -> #122 -> this ticket's new draft recalculator PR. Record the stack URL, PR URL, exact accepted base/head, and predecessor CI result.
- This ticket's implementation commit is accepted ticket 1 in the new PR layer. Each layer contains at most ten accepted ticket commits; the next completed ticket after each tenth commit begins and submits a new draft layer.
- Work may continue locally while CI runs, but this ticket is not pushed until the preceding pushed #122 head is green.

## Implementation

Production jobs publish one answer owned by the job; no production JobEffects reports multiple derivations, while every read, claim, roster, hash and finality operation still pays for DerivationId machinery. The parked fz-kdt.68 experiment measured a 6–10 percent regression and has no production consumer.

Pin current single-answer scheduling semantics, then delete DerivationId, JobDerivation rosters, per-derivation dependency/claim maps, sole-vector construction, publisher wrappers where job identity suffices, withdrawal plumbing, telemetry and tests that exist only for the dormant abstraction. Preserve exact reads, waits, claims, retraction, rebasing, finality, wake attribution and failed-attempt ownership.

## TDD and acceptance

The frozen candidate first proves current publisher ownership and single-answer behavior, then proves the same semantic facts, products, artifacts, failure behavior and runtime output after deletion. Scheduler allocations, hashing and completion work decrease. No experiment switch, counter, parked implementation or stale documentation remains.

The branch contains the exact accepted #121 and #122 histories, contains neither invalid #123 commit, has one real implementation commit titled for this ticket, and has a clean tracked worktree. PR #121 and #122 descriptions name their actual accepted heads, explain their complete current diffs, and contain only current verification evidence. Protected untracked measurements and recoverable stashes remain intact. The new PR is draft, is part of the gh stack above #122, has the required ticket title and explanatory description, and its recorded predecessor CI is green. A fresh ticket-scoped cold adversarial review accepts the code and documentation before commit/close.

Closing this ticket exposes fz-kdt.213 and fz-kdt.188. Generic grounded support, source/failure ownership and exact-edge wait work are therefore built on the final publisher identity.
title: Rebuild the stack on one publisher identity
